messages.content:
RoadDraft is a headless 2D CAD engine for roadway plans. Model space is US survey feet, and a point is [x, y] = [easting, northing] -- the other way round from how coordinates are usually spoken, so N 7300, E 4100 is [4100, 7300]. Sheets are paper inches seen through viewports at a feet-per-inch scale. Work through the commands: each one validates its params and explains what was wrong, every change is journaled and undoable. Start with get_document_state to see what is in the document, list_commands for the full surface, and render_sheet or render_model to look at your work.

To annotate something, find it before you point at it. In a sheet file the design usually lives in a referenced basefile, so the document owns no geometry of its own; find_entities searches the attachments too. Filter by what a thing IS -- layer, type, or its design anchor -- rather than dumping the document: find_entities {anchor: {kind: 'offset', offset: [-15, 15]}, visible_on: 'P-202'} is the pavement edges that sheet shows. Then pass the id straight to place_callout as target_entity, and the engine puts the leader tip on the geometry. Do not compute the point yourself: the midpoint of a curve's endpoints is not on the curve, and roadway linework runs parallel a few feet apart, so a hand-computed point usually lands on the wrong line rather than on nothing. If you do pass a raw target point, read the warning that comes back -- it names what the tip actually touched.

Some things are not entities at all -- a station, a PC, a point at an offset. Ask the design for those: list_alignments with include_references=true names a referenced alignment 'BASE:RTE-7', and station_to_xy, xy_to_station, resolve_anchor and get_design_data all accept that name and answer in host coordinates. To call one out, give place_callout a target_anchor ('86+50@15R', 'PC-2'; BC-2 and EC-2 name the PC and PT too) and that alignment name. Otherwise commands do not take it: nothing can be drawn, labelled or anchored to an alignment this document does not own.

Plan annotation belongs on the sheet, in paper inches, not in the model. Pass the sheet as place_callout's space and still name a model target -- target_entity or target_anchor: the engine sees it through the sheet's viewport (scale and twist included) and puts the tip where it shows on the paper. 'at' then runs along the part of the entity that sheet shows, since a pavement edge runs the whole project and a sheet shows one stretch. find_entities with visible_on gives each row a sheet_point, which is where that tip will land -- use it to choose a position for the text that is clear of the linework. Never work out a viewport by hand: model_to_sheet and sheet_to_model convert, and station_to_xy and point_on_entity take a sheet and answer in paper inches as well.

Drafting from a description works the same way: give the engine the description, not coordinates you worked out. A bearing and distance goes in as written -- create_alignment takes start + legs (each leg a bearing, azimuth or deflection and the distance to the next PI, with the radius of the curve at the PI it starts from), draw_traverse draws lines and curves course by course, and traverse computes the points without drawing. offset_entity copies linework parallel at a distance (one entity, or a chain offset as one path), fillet rounds the corner between two lines with a curve (a curb return), and measure with along gives distances along a line, chain or alignment and square off it. key_points and snap give the exact endpoints, intersections, centers and alignment design points (PI, BC, EC) to build on. Station-and-offset drafting is draw_station_offset with the stations and offsets given ('82+00@15R'). Linework drawn through something is cut back with trim (a point on the part to cut away) or run on with extend, not redrawn from computed points; break, join, lengthen, chamfer, copy, rotate, mirror, scale and array edit what is there. create_points sets COGO points, label_segments letters bearings and distances or L1/C1 tags with line and curve tables, place_along sets blocks or points at an interval, hatch fills an area (a point inside is enough), and area and get_entity read areas, lengths, bearings and curve data off the drawing.

Do one drafting task in a headless CAD engine called RoadDraft, using the tools you have been given. They are your ENTIRE tool surface.

Rules:
- Every change to the drawing must go through a tool call.
- The document is already open and saves itself after each command. Do not save it under another name.
- Nobody can answer questions. Work until you judge the task done, then stop and give your report.
- You have no calculator and no code execution. Any arithmetic you need, do yourself.

THE TASK:
Draft the design model for ELM-AVE. The alignment begins at N 3000.00, E 1000.00, station 10+00. It runs S 80°00'00" E for 800.00 ft to PI-1, where it deflects 40°00'00" to the left on a 500 ft radius curve; then 700.00 ft to PI-2, where it deflects 25°00'00" to the right on a 700 ft radius curve; then 600.00 ft to its end. It has two 11 ft lanes and 5 ft shoulders. Draw the centerline on align_MAIN, the edges of pavement on rd_EP and the outside edges of shoulder on rd_ES, and label the stations every 100 ft.

When finished, reply briefly with:
1. What you created and drew (names, layers, key coordinates).
2. The tool calls that mattered, in order (tool name + the key arguments).
3. Anything that failed, confused you, or that you had to work around -- quote error messages. If you had to compute coordinates yourself, show the arithmetic.

messages.reasoning:
Let's start by understanding the task:

1. Create the alignment ELM-AVE:
   - Starting point: N 3000.00, E 1000.00 → [x, y] = [1000, 3000]
   - Starting station 10+00
   - First leg: S 80°00'00" E, 800.00 ft to PI-1
   - PI-1: 40° left deflection, radius 500
   - Then 700.00 ft to PI-2
   - PI-2: 25° right deflection, radius 700
   - Then 600.00 ft to endpoint

2. Roadway: 11 ft two lanes + 5 ft shoulder. So pavement is 22 ft total width, edge-of-pavement is ±11 ft from centerline. Shoulder extends 5 ft more: ±16 ft.

3. Drawing:
   - Centerline on align_MAIN
   - Edge-of-pavement (±11) on rd_EP
   - Outside edge of shoulder (±16) on rd_ES
   - Station labels every 100 ft

The create_alignment tool takes start + legs. Legs are "one tangent from one PI to the next": direction (one of bearing, azimuth, deflection, angle_right) and distance to the next PI; radius is the curve at the PI at the start of this leg (legs other than the first).

So the legs are:
- Leg 1: bearing "S 80°00'00\" E", distance 800 (to PI-1)
- Leg 2: deflection "40 L", radius 500 (curve at PI-1), distance 700 (to PI-2)
- Leg 3: deflection "25 R", radius 700 (curve at PI-2), distance 600 (to endpoint)

This should compute the PIs automatically.

Next:
- draw_alignment with alignment ELM-AVE, layer align_MAIN
- draw_offset with alignment ELM-AVE, offsets [-11, 11], layer rd_EP
- draw_offset with alignment ELM-AVE, offsets [-16, 16], layer rd_ES
- annotate_stationing with alignment ELM-AVE, interval 100, in model space

First let's check the state of the document. Then create the layers. Then the alignment. Then draw.

Order of operations:
1. get_document_state (summary) — check what's there
2. Create layers: align_MAIN (center, probably), rd_EP, rd_ES
3. Create alignment ELM-AVE with start [1000, 3000], begin_station "10+00", legs
4. draw_alignment to align_MAIN
5. draw_offset [-11, 11] to rd_EP
6. draw_offset [-16, 16] to rd_ES
7. annotate_stationing alignment=ELM-AVE, interval 100, space=model, layer probably align_MAIN or a label layer. The task says "label stations every 100 ft". Use annotate_stationing in model space on the alignment.

Wait — should the stationing annotations be in model space, or on a sheet? The task is "draft the design model of ELM-AVE" and "label stations every 100 ft". Since it's a design model task, model space is fine. The default text height for annotate_stationing in model space is 8 ft.

First let's start with get_document_state.

Note on bearings: "S 80°00'00\" E" — quadrant bearing. The bearing format in the tool accepts "S 80°00'00\" E". Good.

Deflections: "40 L" and "25 R". The deflection field accepts the angle and side, e.g. '33 L'. Radius: leg 2 has radius 500 (curve at PI-1 where leg 2 starts), leg 3 has radius 700 (curve at PI-2 where leg 3 starts).

Let's do the calls. First get_document_state, list_layers, list_alignments in parallel (independent).

Then create layers, create alignment (needs the state first? strictly speaking no, but let's check the state first in case there's existing content).

Let's go.

Actually, for safety, I want to verify the computed geometry after creating the alignment. Using get_design_data kind=curves or tangents I can check bearings/lengths. Good for the report.

Also, let's think about the expected geometry to sanity-check the engine:

Start: E 1000, N 3000, station 10+00.
Leg 1 bearing S 80° E → azimuth = 180 - 80 = 100°. Direction: dx = sin(100°)*800 = 0.98481*800 = 787.85, dy = cos(100°)*800 = -0.17365*800 = -138.92. PI-1: E = 1000 + 787.846 = 1787.846, N = 3000 - 138.923 = 2861.077.

Tangent length at PI-1: T1 = 500 * tan(40°/2) = 500 * tan(20°) = 500 * 0.363970 = 181.985.
Curve 1: delta 40°, R 500, L = 500 * 40° in radians = 500 * 0.698132 = 349.066.

PI-2: PI-1 + 700 ft at new direction (100° + 40° = 140°). dx = sin(140°)*700 = 0.642788*700 = 449.95, dy = cos(140°)*700 = -0.766044*700 = -536.23. PI-2: E = 1787.846 + 449.951 = 2237.797, N = 2861.077 - 536.231 = 2324.846.

T2 = 700 * tan(12.5°) = 700 * 0.221694 = 155.186.
Curve 2: L = 700 * 25° in radians = 700 * 0.436332 = 305.433.

Endpoint: PI-2 + 600 ft at 140° + (-25°) = 115°. dx = sin(115°)*600 = 0.906308*600 = 543.78, dy = cos(115°)*600 = -0.422618*600 = -253.57. Endpoint: E = 2237.797 + 543.785 = 2781.582, N = 2324.846 - 253.571 = 2071.275.

Raw station of endpoint: 800 + 349.066 + 700 + 305.433 + 600 = 2754.50. So end station = 10+00 + 2754.50 = 12+754.50 → display is 13+54.50? Wait: 10+00 = raw 1000. Total raw = 1000 + 2754.499 = 3754.499 → display 37+54.50? Hmm wait.

Hold on. Starting station 10+00 = raw 1000 ft. Total length of alignment: 800 (tangent 1) + 349.066 (curve 1) + 700 (tangent 2) + 305.433 (curve 2) + 600 (tangent 3) = 2754.499. End raw station = 1000 + 2754.499 = 3754.499 → display station 37+54.50.

PC-1 raw = 1000 + 800 - 181.985 = 1618.015 → 16+18.01 (display 16+18.01).
PT-1 raw = 1618.015 + 349.066 = 1967.081 → 19+67.08.
PC-2 raw = 1967.081 + 700 - 155.186 = 2511.895 → 25+11.90 (display 25+11.89? Let me recompute: 2511.895 → 25+11.895 ≈ 25+11.90).
PT-2 raw = 2511.895 + 305.433 = 2817.328 → 28+17.33.
End raw = 2817.328 + 600 = 3417.328??

Hmm, that contradicts. Let me recompute. 1000 + 800 = 1800 at PI-1. Then curve 1: PC-1 = 1800 - 181.985 = 1618.015. PT-1 = 1618.015 + 349.066 = 1967.081. PI-2 = 1967.081 + 700 = 2667.081. PC-2 = 2667.081 - 155.186 = 2511.895. PT-2 = 2511.895 + 305.433 = 2817.328. End = 2817.328 + 600 = 3417.328.

So end station display = 34+17.33. Total length = 2417.328 = 800+349.066+700+305.433+600 = 2754.499? No wait: 800 + 349.066 = 1149.066; +700 = 1849.066; +305.433 = 2154.499; +600 = 2754.499. But 3417.328 - 1000 = 2417.328. Mismatch!

Let me recheck: T1 = 181.985, L1 = 349.066. PI-1 is at 1800. PC-1 = 1800 - 181.985 = 1618.015. OK. PT-1 = 1618.015 + 349.066 = 1967.081. Check: PT-1 = PI-1 + T1... no: PT-1 = PI-1 + L - T = 1800 + 349.066 - 181.985 = 1967.081. ✓. Then tangent 2 is from PT-1 to PI-2 = 700: PI-2 = 2667.081. ✓. PC-2 = 2667.081 - 155.186 = 2511.895. PT-2 = 2511.895 + 305.433 = 2817.328. End = 2817.328 + 600 = 3417.328.

Total: (1800 - 1618.015) + (1967.081 - 1618.015) + (2667.081 - 1967.081) + (2817.328 - 2511.895) + (3417.328 - 2817.328) = 181.985 + 349.066 + 700 + 305.433 + 600 = 2136.484? No: 181.985 + 349.066 = 531.051; +700 = 1231.051; +305.433 = 1536.484; +600 = 2136.484. Hmm, that's the sum of the tangent 1 partial + ... no, that's wrong. Total length = 3417.328 - 1000 = 2417.328. And the sum of the elements should equal that: T1 (800) + C1 (349.066) + T2 (700) + C2 (305.433) + T3 (600) = 2754.499. But 2417.328 ≠ 2754.499. Difference is 337.171.

Something is off. Ah! I see the bug: in the element sum, T1 = 800 is the full tangent from start to PI-1, but the alignment length includes PC-1 at 1618.015, i.e., 618.015 on tangent 1, then curve 349.066... no wait. Alignment length = (PC-1 - start) + C1 + (PT-1 + ... hmm, no.

Elements of the alignment: tangent from 1000 to 1618.015 (length 618.015), curve 1 (349.066), tangent from 1967.081 to 2511.895 (length 544.814), curve 2 (305.433), tangent from 2817.328 to 3417.328 (length 600). Total = 618.015 + 349.066 + 544.814 + 305.433 + 600 = 2417.328. ✓

I was mistakenly using 800 for the first element tangent. The element tangent is shorter because the curve starts T before the PI. So end station = 34+17.33, total length 2417.33 ft. Good — the engine computes all this, but it's good to have a sanity check.

Display: start 10+00, end 34+17.33. Stations every 100 ft: 10+00, 11+00, ..., 34+00.

OK, let's start executing. First parallel call round: get_document_state, list_layers, list_alignments.

messages.reasoning:
The document is in a clean state. Layers align_MAIN, rd_EP, and rd_ES already exist. Next, I'll create an alignment from start point + legs.

Start point: N 3000.00, E 1000.00 → [1000, 3000], starting station 10+00.

Legs:
1. Bearing S 80°00'00" E, distance 800.00 (to PI-1)
2. Deflection 40° left, R=500 at PI-1, then 700.00 ft to PI-2 — leg 2 is the tangent from PI-1 to PI-2.
3. Deflection 25° right, R=700 at PI-2, then 600.00 ft to the end — leg 3 is the tangent from PI-2 to the end point.

Therefore:
- Leg 1: {bearing: "S 80°00'00\" E", distance: 800}
- Leg 2: {deflection: "40 L", radius: 500, distance: 700}
- Leg 3: {deflection: "25 R", radius: 700, distance: 600}

After that, I'll draw the alignment to align_MAIN, draw the offsets [-11, 11] on rd_EP (two 11 ft lanes = 22 ft wide pavement, so ±11), and draw the offsets [-16, 16] on rd_ES (5 ft shoulder → outer edge is 11+5 = 16).

Next, on the alignment I'll annotate the stationing at 100 ft intervals.

Alright, I'll create the alignment now.

messages.reasoning:
Wait a minute—the engine says PI-2 [1787.85, 2861.08] R=500?? It looks like it treated the leg with deflection "40 L" as... Hmm: "PI-2 [1787.85, 2861.08] R=500, PI-3 [2394.06, 3211.08] R=700". The radius 500 curve should be at PI-1 (the one where the first leg begins). And the PI-1 coordinate [1612.15, 2861.08] should be where the first leg ends. Let me check: the endpoint of leg 1 should be [1000 + 800·cos(100°), 3000 + 800·sin(100°)] = [1000 + 800·(−0.173648), 3000 + 800·(0.984808)] = [1000 − 138.919, 3000 + 787.846] = [861.081, 2787.846]...

Wait, that doesn't match either. Let me recompute. Hmm, azimuth 100°: cos(100°) = −0.173648, sin(100°) = 0.984808. ΔE = 800 × −0.173648 = −138.92 → E = 1000 − 138.92 = 861.08. ΔN = 800 × 0.984808 = +787.85 → N = 3787.85.

So PI-1 should be [861.08, 3787.85]. But the engine reports PI-2 [1787.85, 2861.08]?? That's weird: [1787.85, 2861.08]—interestingly: 1787.85 = 1000 + 787.85 (that's the northing value I computed!), 2861.08 = 3000 − 138.92 (that's my easting!). So the engine swapped x and y: it took [x, y] = [easting, northing] = [1000, 3000]... and then ran the bearing with E/N swapped?

Hmm, wait. Let me look again: reported PI-2 = [1787.85, 2861.08]. If x=easting: E=1787.85, N=2861.08. My computed E=861.08, N=3787.85. Hmm, 1787.85 = 1000+787.85; 2861.08 = 3000−138.92. So engine's E = startE + ΔN (mine), engine's N = startN − ΔE (mine). That's as if the engine rotated... let me think: if I used azimuth 100° but measured the direction as (sin, cos)... direction (sin(az), cos(az)) = (0.984808, −0.173648): ΔE=+787.85, ΔN=−138.92. That would give [1787.85, 2861.08]. So the engine used (sin az, cos az)?? That's a rotation of the direction: equivalent to interpreting the azimuth as... if I use (sin az, cos az) instead of (cos az, sin az): that's az' such that cos(az')=sin(az), sin(az')=cos(az) → az' = 90° − az = −10° → azimuth 350°. That means the engine treated my bearing as if... hmm, 90° − 100° = −10° → 350°.

Or: the engine interpreted "S 80°00'00\" E" as azimuth 100° correctly, but then interpreted x as northing and y as easting? If the engine's point convention is [northing, easting] and I passed [1000, 3000] thinking it was [E, N]... then engine's N=1000, E=3000, and with the correct formula endpoint: E = 3000 − 138.92 = 2861.08, N = 1000 + 787.85 = 1787.85 → [N, E] = [1787.85, 2861.08] → which is exactly what was reported as [x, y]! So the engine interpreted my [1000, 3000] as [N, E] = N 1000, E 3000.

But the tool description explicitly says: "x is easting and y is northing, so N 7300, E 4100 is [4100, 7300]". And create_alignment's start: "[x, y] = [easting, northing]". And the system prompt repeats this too. Yet the result indicates the opposite behavior... or did I make a calculation error?

Let me very carefully recompute. S 80° E: quadrant southeast, 80° from south toward east. Direction vector: south is (E:0, N:−1); east is (E:+1, N:0). Rotating 80° from south toward east: E component = sin(80°) = 0.984808, N component = −cos(80°) = −0.173648. ΔE = +787.85, ΔN = −138.92.

Wait! I made a sign error in the quadrant decomposition earlier! S 80° E: measured from the south line toward east. The southward component is cos(80°), the eastward component is sin(80°). 80° is close to east, so mostly east, slightly south. Yes: ΔE = +787.85, ΔN = −138.92.

I confused myself earlier with the azimuth formula. Azimuth 100°: direction (E, N) = (cos(100°), sin(100°))?? No. Azimuth θ is measured clockwise from north. North = (E:0, N:+1). Rotating clockwise (as seen in the standard E-N plane with E right, N up, clockwise means... from north toward east): rotating 90° clockwise gives east (E:+1, N:0). The general formula: direction = (sin θ, cos θ). At θ=100°: (sin100°, cos100°) = (0.984808, −0.173648) = (E:+0.9848, N:−0.1736). Yes!! ΔE = +787.85, ΔN = −138.92.

The error was in applying the (cos, sin) formula—azimuth uses (sin θ, cos θ) in the (E, N) components. I had that right the first time (ΔE +787.85, ΔN −138.92) and then got confused and "corrected" it wrongly. The engine is correct: PI-1 = [1787.85, 2861.08] = [E 1787.85, N 2861.08].

So the engine's numbering: PI-2 is at [1787.85, 2861.08]?? The message says "PIs BEGIN [1000, 3000], PI-2 [1787.85, 2861.08] R=500, PI-3 [2394.06, 3211.08] R=700, END [2991.78, 3263.37]". Hmm, so it labels the first PI (where the R=500 curve is) as "PI-2"—probably because PI-1 is BEGIN (some conventions count BEGIN as PI-1). So their PI-2 = my PI-1 ✓, their PI-3 = my PI-2 = [2394.06, 3211.08] ✓ (matches my hand calc [2394.06, 3211.08]), END = [2991.78, 3263.37] ✓ (matches my calc [2991.78, 3263.37]).

Length 2080.16 ft ✓ (my total 2080.174). End station 30+80.16 ✓.

Good—no error in the engine, my initial hand calc was correct and I got myself confused midway. The alignment is fine.

Next: check design data, then draw. Let me check the curves/tangents to see the PC/PT/MC stations and bearings.

After that:
2. draw_alignment alignment=ELM-AVE layer=align_MAIN
3. draw_offset alignment=ELM-AVE offsets [-16, 16] layer=rd_EP
4. draw_offset alignment=ELM-AVE offsets [-11, 11]... wait—offsets: pavement edges ±11, shoulder outer edges ±16. Two calls:
   - draw_offset offsets [-11, 11] layer rd_EP
   - draw_offset offsets [-16, 16] layer rd_ES
5. annotate_stationing alignment=ELM-AVE interval=100 space=model

Then render the model to check, and if needed check the sheet... the task is just design model, no sheet needed. Render the model for a visual check.

First, let me pull get_design_data for the curves to report in my summary. Actually, I can fold that in: call draw_alignment, the two draw_offsets, annotate_stationing, and get_design_data all... these are mostly independent: drawing doesn't depend on the design data. But the annotate_stationing alignment mode uses the design; independent of the drawing. All five can be run in one block: get_design_data (curves), draw_alignment, draw_offset EP, draw_offset ES, annotate_stationing.

Wait—annotate_stationing default text size: text_height default is 8 ft (or the annotation scale × 0.10 in)—annotation scale is null → fixed 8 ft default. Tick half-length default 3.5 ft. label_offset default 6 ft below. That's fine for the model.

Station labels every 100 ft: 10+00 to 30+00, ticks every 100 ft. Caltrans lettering default: the full number at every 500 ft (10, 15, 20, 25, 30) and the units digit elsewhere. Good.
